engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Tactics: The Fork
chess.body: A fork attacks two pieces simultaneously with one piece. Knight forks are the deadliest — they move in an L-shape and cannot be blocked. Look for squares your knight can reach that simultaneously attack king + queen, or rook + rook. Practice: set up NxC5+ forking king and rook. Classic beginner trap.

wisdom.title: Letting Go of Control
wisdom.body: You can control your effort. You cannot control outcomes. The job market, the Instagram algorithm, the baby's sleep schedule — all outside your control. Epictetus: 'Seek not that the things which happen should happen as you wish; but wish the things which happen to be as they are, and you will have a tranquil flow of life.'

book.author: James Clear
book.chapter: The Four Laws of Behaviour Change
book.lesson: Every habit is built on four components: Cue (make it obvious) → Craving (make it attractive) → Response (make it easy) → Reward (make it satisfying). To build a good habit, apply all four. To break a bad one, invert them: make it invisible, make it unattractive, make it difficult, make it unsatisfying. The two-minute rule: when starting a new habit, it should take less than two minutes. You're not running 5km yet — you're putting on your running shoes. The gateway habit becomes the habit.
book.key_quote: Reduce friction for good habits. Increase friction for bad ones.
book.action: Apply the two-minute rule to one habit you've been failing to start. Make the first step so small it's impossible to say no.
crux: You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems.
1% better daily compounds to 37x in a year. 1% worse decays to 0.03x.
Habits form on a four-step loop: cue → craving → response → reward.
Build good habits: make it obvious, attractive, easy, satisfying. Invert all four to break one.
Identity drives behaviour, not the reverse. 'I don't smoke' beats 'I'm trying to quit'.
Every action is a vote for the person you are becoming. Majority wins, not unanimity.
The two-minute rule: a new habit must take under two minutes to start.
Environment beats willpower. Motivation is overrated; friction is decisive.
Habit stacking: after [existing habit], I will [new habit]. The old habit becomes the cue.
You need a plateau of latent potential. Results lag effort — most people quit inside the lag.
Never miss twice. One miss is an accident. Two is the start of a new habit.
Measure what you want to repeat. An unrecorded habit drifts within three weeks.
learnings: Discipline is a design problem, not a character problem.
The gap between effort and visible result is where nearly everyone quits.
Systems survive bad days. Motivation does not.
Tracking is not admin. Tracking is the habit.
examples: British Cycling went from one Tour de France win in 110 years to five in six years by stacking 1% gains — pillow hygiene, hand-washing, bike paint for dust visibility.
Clear's own recovery: a bat to the face at 15, two years of rebuilding, then an academic All-American — built entirely on sleep and study routines, not talent.
Twice-weekly gym attendance beats a 90-minute session once a month, even though the monthly total is similar. Frequency builds identity; volume does not.
adapt: Score one caption per day before posting. The score is the habit, not the post.
Two-minute rule on the Dubai job hunt: open the tracker and add one company. That is the whole commitment.
SIP on auto-debit the day salary lands. Remove the monthly decision entirely.
Never miss twice on the daily brief. One skipped morning is fine. Two means the system broke.

minimalism.title: Travel Light As Practice
minimalism.body: Pack for a week in a carry-on. It teaches, in three days, exactly how little you require — a lesson that transfers directly home.
minimalism.action: Next trip: carry-on only. Note what you never opened.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: The Right Hand Rule
etiquette.body: In the Gulf and much of Asia, give and receive with the right hand — cards, food, documents, money. The left hand carries a specific connotation. This is not a preference; it is the baseline.
etiquette.action: Hand over your next document or card with the right hand, deliberately.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: The First Hour Is Yours
stillness.body: Whoever touches your attention first sets the agenda for the day. If that is a notification, you have outsourced the day to a stranger's priorities before you were fully awake.
stillness.action: No screen for the first 30 minutes tomorrow. Nothing else changes.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Availability Heuristic
model.body: You judge probability by how easily an example comes to mind. Plane crashes feel likelier than car crashes because they are memorable, not because they are common.
model.action: Check one belief against actual frequency data rather than recall.
model.label: Mental Model

arabic.use: Before an exam, an interview, a launch. Sincere and common.
arabic.label: Arabic

drill.title: Explain It To A Ten-Year-Old
drill.body: Take the most technical thing you know and explain it with no jargon. If you cannot, you have memorised it rather than understood it. This is the Feynman technique and it is brutal.
drill.action: Pick one concept. Explain it in writing with no technical terms.
drill.label: Drill

health.title: Heat And Cold Are Adjuncts, Not Basics
health.body: Sauna shows dose-dependent cardiovascular association in Finnish cohorts. Cold has weaker evidence and may blunt hypertrophy if taken right after lifting. Neither substitutes for training and sleep.
health.action: Only add these once training, sleep, and protein are consistent.
health.label: Health

quote.name: Sam Walton
quote.quote: High expectations are the key to everything.

case.title: Stripe: Developer-First, CEO-Last
case.story: Stripe built payment APIs for developers, not CFOs. 7 lines of code to accept payments. No sales team for the first 3 years — product sold itself.
case.lesson: The best distribution is built into the product. If developers love it, adoption spreads through word of mouth. Sell to builders, not buyers.

fpna.title: Three-Statement Model
fpna.body: P&L → Balance Sheet → Cash Flow — they must tie. If they don't, you have a bug.

cfo.title: FC Step 3: Internal Controls
cfo.body: A Controller without strong controls is a liability. Know COSO framework. Segregation of duties. Maker-checker in AP/AR. SOX lite for listed companies. Document your controls. Auditors love documented processes.

money_hack.title: Emergency Fund
money_hack.body: 6 months of expenses in a liquid FD. Job loss + medical can overlap.

dubai.title: What a Financial Controller title actually needs
dubai.body: The jump from FP&A Manager to Controller in the Gulf is statutory reporting plus audit ownership plus a team. If the CV has no signed statutory set on it, that is the gap — not the years.
dubai.targets: Controller bands start around AED 40K. It is the next rung, and it is close.
dubai.action: Get a statutory reporting line on the CV in the next six months. Any entity, any size.

desk.productivity: Use Parkinson's Law: shorter deadlines. Work expands to fill time given.

father.title: Build then let her destroy
father.do: Stack three blocks, let her knock them down, rebuild. Repeat until she loses interest.
father.why: Cause and effect is the entire lesson. Knocking down precedes building by months — do not rush to the constructive half.

father.title: Do bedtime alone once this week
father.do: Handle the entire routine solo — no handover, no rescue.
father.why: Solo caregiving builds a distinct relationship rather than an assisted one. It also gives her mother an uninterrupted evening, which is not a small thing at seven months.

life_wisdom.teaching: The third jewel, and deliberately placed after right perception and right knowledge — you cannot act well on a false picture.
life_wisdom.apply: When a decision feels hard, check whether it is genuinely a conduct problem or actually a perception problem you have not resolved. Most are the latter.

life_wisdom.teaching: Effort is one of the eight, but so is rightness of effort. Energy in the wrong direction is not neutral; it entrenches the error.
life_wisdom.apply: Before adding hours to a problem, spend ten minutes asking whether the problem is the right one. Most overwork is misdirection, not insufficiency.

vocab.note: Also technical — contingent liabilities are disclosed, not recognised.

speaking.title: Read a wire story aloud
speaking.drill: Take one headline from the World section and read the first paragraph aloud, twice.
speaking.why: Journalistic prose is tightly written. Reading it aloud daily rewires sentence rhythm faster than conversation does.

interview_tech.q: Like-for-like sales are +3% but total sales are −2%. What is happening?
interview_tech.a: The existing estate is growing while the total base shrank — you closed stores, or a material store left the LFL set. LFL strips out openings and closures, so the gap is the net space effect. Ask: was the closure deliberate portfolio pruning, in which case −2% total with +3% LFL and better margin is a good outcome; or did leases expire without replacement, which is a pipeline failure. Follow with sales density per sqm — that tells you whether the remaining estate is genuinely stronger.

interview_tech.q: You are consolidating Malaysia and Indonesia. Where do FX translation differences land?
interview_tech.a: Functional currency results are translated at the closing rate for assets and liabilities, average rate for P&L, and the difference goes to other comprehensive income as a foreign currency translation reserve — not through P&L. It only recycles to P&L on disposal of the foreign operation. The trap: intercompany balances that are effectively permanent investment belong in the net investment, so their FX also goes to OCI. Getting that wrong puts noise through earnings every quarter.

interview_soft.q: Tell me about a time you had to say no to a business partner.
interview_soft.a: Retail finance says no constantly — to a buy outside open-to-buy, a promotion that destroys margin, a headcount request without a business case. Pick one and show the method: you did not just refuse, you showed the number that made it a no, and you offered what would make it a yes. The best answers end with the partner coming back with a version you could approve, because that proves the relationship survived.

Be concrete or it sounds rehearsed. Good answers name the specific texture of the work: seeing a decision you modelled play out in real numbers weeks later, building a team member into something they were not when they arrived, or the particular satisfaction of a clean close. Avoid 'challenge' and 'growth' unqualified. If money genuinely is a driver — Dubai, young family — it is fine to say it is one of several, and honest beats performed modesty.
